pairs.question: Quis deus hos ira tristi contendere iussit?
pairs.derivation: Authorial rhetorical question (line numbered 9 in raw text) immediately self-answered. The question is the full interrogative line. The answer is the operative naming phrase 'Latonae et magni proles Iouis' (Apollo), cut at the first full stop; what follows ('Ille Pelasgum infestam regi pestem...') is narrative elaboration on what the god did, not part of the identification answer.

pairs.question: Quae te terra uirum, qui te genuere parentes?
pairs.answer: Hesiona de matre uides Telamone creatum, nobilis est domus et fama generosa propago.
pairs.derivation: Hector asks Ajax his land and parentage; introduced by the framing 'Tunc bello maximus Hector:' which is dropped. The following line 'Viribus es proles generosa atque inclita - dixit -' is a separate complimentary statement plus speech tag, not part of the interrogative, so it is excluded. Ajax's reply is introduced by the framing 'At contra se ferre parat Telamonius Aiax:' (dropped); the two-line answer directly states his parentage and house. Stops there; what follows (Hector recognizing Hesione's name and proposing they cease fighting) is the next move, not the answer.
